title: Ecosystem Interchange Study: Model API Stability and Enterprise Renewal Impact
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Research and quantify the relationship between model API stability (breaking changes, deprecations, semantic drift in outputs, performance regressions) and enterprise renewal/expansion behavior. Produce a reproducible analysis, an internal dashboard, and an operational playbook that sales/AMs and SREs can use to mitigate churn risk tied to third-party model changes.
context: Commercial customers often cite 'model regressions' and 'breaking API changes' in renewal conversations. We lack an empirically-backed framework that ties measurable API-change signals to churn/renewal outcomes and competitor versioning practices. Several enterprise losses in 2025 referenced model compatibility headaches during a migration window.
goals: 1) Establish a signal taxonomy for API-level stability (breaking change frequency, deprecation windows, semantic output drift metrics, latency variance). 2) Link those signals to renewal cohorts using survival and regression analyses. 3) Produce a dashboard and a mitigation playbook with prescriptive triggers for sales/SRE. 4) Competitive scan: map top 8 model providers' versioning cadence and documented migration costs.
success_criteria: 1) Statistically significant association (p<0.05) between at least one API-stability signal and a change in renewal probability in historical cohorts. 2) A reproducible ETL and dashboard ingesting renewal + changelog signals updated daily. 3) Playbook with 3 prescriptive interventions (canary routing, automatic fallback mapping, commercial credit templates) validated by one internal dry-run. 4) Competitive matrix with vendor cadence and migration effort scores for the top 8 providers.
out_of_scope: Deep code-level compatibility for each model family, building production automated rollback tooling (we will instead hand off recommendations to Eng), and long-term legal/contract renegotiation strategy (we will surface templates but defer negotiations to GTM/legal).
timeline: Week 0 (kickoff): finalize signals and data access. Week 1-2: ingest telemetry, changelogs, and contract/renewal data; conduct interviews with 10 AMs. Week 3: run survival analysis and probit regressions; build dashboard prototype. Week 4: complete playbook, competitive scan, and stakeholder review. Deliver final report and handoff to Eng/Sales by due_date.
stakeholders: R&D - Model Ops (ENG lead: Samir Gupta)
deliverables: operational playbook (Confluence) - mitigation templates + SLA language examples
competitive vendor cadence matrix (spreadsheet) - drive link TBD
risks: 1) Renewal data is siloed by region and requires legal approval for cross-team analysis. 2) Signal noise: short-term regressions may not be causal to churn. 3) Competitive vendor changelog transparency varies; some providers do not publish sufficient history.
notes: We will attempt to standardize changelog semantics into three buckets: structural API changes (breaking), documented deprecations (non-breaking but requiring migration), and behavioral drift (latency/quality regressions measured via eval suites). Use existing Redwood Optimize eval-set harness where possible.
